<description>
`ScriptCompression::Unser` ignores the `DecompressScript` return value and
leaves the script empty on failure, without notifying upper layers about the error.
In the worst-case scenario, which is currently only reachable through corruption,
an unspendable off-curve P2PK turns into an anyone-can-spend empty script.
Given that, properly throwing the error to prevent any future mistakes from
happening seems the sanest path to follow.

Aside from that, added coverage for a P2PK script with an uncompressed pubkey
that has a valid X but a wrong Y, which makes it unspendable. Checking we store
such scripts raw and never encode them as 0x04/0x05, as those encodings
serialize X with only Y's parity (not the full Y), which would make decompression
recompute Y from X and turn the unspendable script into a spendable one, which
would not be good.
</description>

`DecompressScript` can only fail for types 4 and 5, when libsecp256k1 rejects `02/03 || x`: x is not below p, or x³+7 is not a square. Inside `Unser` the type is always below 6, so the final `return false` is unreachable and the new throw fires on exactly those inputs. I checked this against 4636 vectors from a library I maintain, cross-checked there with Euler's criterion: 2398 throw and 2238 decode to the expected script, as a bare script, inside a `Coin` and inside a `CTxUndo`, with the trailing byte left in the stream each time. The vectors include 200 x+p values, 101 of them reducing to a valid x; all throw, since libsecp256k1 requires x < p.

On regtest, a snapshot whose first coin is rewritten as type 4 with x=5 (off the curve) or x=1+p fails `loadtxoutset` with "Bad snapshot format or truncated snapshot after deserializing 0 coins", while x=1 still reaches the content hash check. `compress_tests`, `coins_tests` and the `script` fuzz target (3000 random inputs, non-libFuzzer build) pass. I measured on macOS at the PR head with a unit test reading the vectors and a functional test, which I can share as a gist.

The throw also reaches the coins cursor, where a rollback `dumptxoutset` skips the unreadable coin and `scantxoutset` returns partial results as if cancelled. I did not test those paths, but l0rinc's diff for them would fit in this PR.
